column1: # Every settings key and the description it has now: <file> TAB <path> TAB <description>.
# TestDescriptionsAreRecordedWhenTheyChange compares it with the schemas. Do not edit it by hand:
# change the description in the schema, keep the old text in Previous, then run

column3: MCP endpoint of the server this machine talks to. The first connect seeds it from CARTOGRAPHER_SERVER_URL when that is set.
Name under which the server is registered in each agent's MCP configuration.
The server requires a bearer token; the clients then send the token.

The bearer token: ${NAME} reads it from the environment variable NAME (an unattended run falls back to the private token file `connect` wrote), anything else is the token itself, and the file is then kept private (mode 0600). The agents' MCP entries can only name a variable, so a literal token has them read $CARTOGRAPHER_TOKENS.

Accept a plain http:// server.url that is not loopback, sending the bearer token in clear. Off by default: the client refuses such a URL. Set by `connect --allow-insecure-http`; CARTOGRAPHER_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1 allows one run.

The access mode of a folder under no workspace binding ($HOME included), for every provider: read gives the provider's KBs with no write tool; write gives them read-write, still with no KB artifact (artifacts stay tied to a binding). A provider's own providers.<provider>.unbound_access beats it, and it beats the built-in read. Any other value is read. It only matters for a provider whose MCP entry is the workspace bridge (it has a binding); not a security boundary.

The settings of each connected provider, as <provider>: {kbs, scope, unbound_access, config_dirs, access, tools, allow_symlinks, workspaces}. kbs is the KBs the provider receives; a provider with no entry, or an entry without kbs, receives every known KB (edit it with `cartographer client`). scope is where it receives KB artifacts: provider puts them under the home directory and gives every session every KB the provider receives, read-write, wherever it starts (the default; nothing moves until a provider is switched); workspace makes the folder decide: a bound folder gets its KBs with their artifacts, any other folder ($HOME included) gets the provider's KBs read-only unless unbound_access says write, and no artifact either way. A repository a KB declares in its paths.yaml is bound to that KB automatically (a derived binding, recomputed by every sync and not stored in this file). unbound_access (read or write) is the mode of a folder under no binding for this provider and beats defaults.unbound_access. config_dirs lists extra Claude Code config directories (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) whose .claude.json also receives the MCP entry; claude only. access: read with tools: minimal connects the provider read-only with the minimal tool list (written by `connect --access read-min`; remove both keys to clear it). allow_symlinks lists links that writes may follow (off by default, a symlinked config is otherwise refused): each entry is the link itself (~ and $HOME are expanded), a listed directory link covers everything below it, a link nested below a listed one needs its own entry, and the link is kept while the write lands on its target; it is read only from this file in the home directory, never from a project-level file in a repository, and `cartographer client symlinks <provider>` edits it. workspaces is which KBs the provider receives in a given directory, as [{path, kbs}]: the deepest binding wins, a folder under no binding is read-only unless unbound_access says write, and these are the explicit bindings (the derived ones are not stored here; an entry on a declared repository's path replaces the derived binding, kbs: [] opts it out on this machine and bind: false in the KB's paths.yaml for everyone).

The settings of each KB on this machine, applied to every provider, as <kb>: {access, artifacts, identity, signing_keys}; default holds the identity of every KB without an entry of its own. artifacts: false stops sync from provisioning that KB's skills, subagents, hooks and MCP descriptors: the ones already installed are removed at the next sync, and its skills line and subagent sentence leave the instruction block. The KB stays connected: its MCP tools and routing sentence remain. It wins over every scope and binding and never adds a KB to any of them; absent, or true, is the default. It has no effect on a server that does not name its KBs. access: read connects that KB read-only on every provider that receives it, while the provider's other KBs stay writable; write, or absent, is the default. It is a scope filter, not a security boundary (a client that edits its own URL drops it): hard isolation is a server token role (kb:<name>:r). It needs a server with a routed endpoint. Edit both with `cartographer client kb`. identity is the git author of this machine's writes to the KB, Name <email>; without one, the identity git resolves in the session's repository, and an empty value sends no author, so the server names the token. signing_keys are the Ed25519 public keys pinned to verify the signed artifacts the KB serves; pins are configured out of band, never learned from a sync.

The plugins installed on this machine. Written by the plugin commands, not by hand: source is a git remote or an absolute folder, ref the branch, tag or commit asked for, sha the commit it resolved to, installed and approved the digests of the fetched and of the approved tree (approved empty is pending), enabled and settings what the user chose.

Directories scanned, 4 levels deep, for git clones to resolve {{repo:<key>}} placeholders; a root that does not exist is skipped. A key with an entry in placeholders.paths is never searched. The scan also finds the repositories that derived workspace bindings bind.
Manual name-to-directory mapping for {{path:<name>}}, and an override for {{repo:<key>}}. Edit it with `cartographer paths set`.
Placeholder ids known to be absent on this machine, for example repo:work-tools; sync stops reporting them. Edit it with `cartographer paths ignore`.

Set by the first sync, which approves the hooks and executable artifacts already installed with the content the KB serves now. Never cleared, so a revoked approval is not granted again. Do not edit by hand.
Look up the latest release once a day and tell when a newer one exists. false makes no lookup at all. The client never replaces itself.
Scan session transcripts to tell the server which skills and agents this machine loads. false reads no transcript and reports no usage.
Listen address of the HTTP transport, for example :39273. Empty serves MCP over stdio.
Directory whose direct subdirectories are discovered as KBs, and where remote KBs are cloned. The name credentials is the server's own and is never discovered.

Directory with every secret file, looked up by KB name: <kb>.ssh, <kb>.token and <kb>.age (each with a default.* for the KBs without their own), <kb>.signing (the artifact signing seed, no default) and known_hosts (one file for every remote). On Kubernetes it is one mounted Secret (defaultMode 0440 with the pod's fsGroup). A file readable by other users, or by the group when it is the server's own, is warned about once at start.

Look up the latest release once a day and report it in /health and kb_status when it is newer; the Atlas reads the release history from the same GitHub list when someone opens it. Off, the server makes neither call. A dev build never checks.

Run the safe repairs of every KB in the background, once a day and after a pull that changed it. false stops that timer only: repair on write, the write gate and kb_repair are not affected. While a live Surveyor declaring the repair task keeps repairing a KB, the timer skips that KB.
Bearer-token authentication of the HTTP transport. auto turns it on when at least one token is configured.

Bearer tokens: a bare string (admin, every KB) or a mapping with token, scopes (kb:<name>:r or kb:<name>:rw), roles, id, kind (human, client or surveyor) expires_at (RFC 3339; required for client and surveyor, which are never admin) and proxy (true for the bearer of the SSO proxy of auth.proxy_identity). A token may be written ${NAME} to read it from the environment. A running server picks up a changed list without a restart, at the next poll of the file or on SIGHUP (auth.reload_interval).

Named permission sets that tokens reference by name; each has a name and rules (kb, access r or rw, and optional maps, journals, types, artifacts: r to withhold the skill, agent and hook write tools from a rule that otherwise writes, and secrets: none to withhold the secret tools and the concept fields that point at a secret). A running server picks up a change without a restart.

Per-user identity behind an SSO proxy. The proxy authenticates with a token declared proxy: true (never admin; its scopes or roles are the ceiling of every person behind it) and names the person in a header; the server believes the header only from trusted_addresses and on that token. The groups map to roles through group_roles. A running server picks up a change without a restart.
CIDRs (or addresses) of the proxy's TCP peer; required. A /0 prefix is refused and loopback is not implied. X-Forwarded-For is never used.
Header carrying the person's name; required. The proxy must overwrite it on every inbound request. At most 128 bytes, printable, no angle brackets.
Header carrying the person's groups (at most 64 of 128 bytes); without it nobody maps to a role.
Separator of the groups header.
Group name to the roles it grants. A person's permissions are the union of their groups' roles, clamped by the proxy token's own; no mapped group is a 403.

How often a running server looks at the config file for a changed auth section (tokens, roles) and applies it without a restart. 0 stops the polling; SIGHUP reloads at any time. A reload that fails validation, or that changes the auth mode, is refused and the tokens in force are kept.

The KBs to clone and mount: each entry has a remote. A KB that is a folder under data is discovered and needs no entry. KBs from CARTOGRAPHER_KB_REMOTES are added to this list (bare remotes: name and branch need the file).
Git remote a KB is cloned from, under data. A KB with a remote syncs with it; one without never contacts anything.
KB name, in place of the one derived from the remote. It drives the endpoint, the token scopes, the clone directory and the names of the KB's files in credentials_dir.

Branch this server alone commits and pushes to, in place of the KB's own branch setting (which is then not read); the first push creates it. Empty keeps the KB's setting, and without one the remote's default branch. Only here, in the file: CARTOGRAPHER_KB_REMOTES has no per-entry option.

The git identity, Name <email>, the server commits as, per KB name; the key default stands for every KB without an entry. A present empty entry means that KB has none and commits as the server identity. The identities are the author and the committer of the commits the server makes with no writer of their own (the unattended repair, merges, conflict resolution) and of a write whose client sends no valid Cartographer-Author. Set one when the remote's forge rejects commits whose author or committer is not one of its accounts. Without an entry the server identity applies, Cartographer <cartographer@host>.
Path of the append-only operation log, which is always on and signed with audit.key from credentials_dir (generated at the first start). Empty keeps it at <data>/audit/audit.log.

With best_effort a failed append is logged and the call carries on, and a log or key the server cannot open is a warning at start; with required the call is rejected before the tool runs, and the server does not start without its signed log.
Size after which the active log segment is rotated (64 MiB by default), so retention has segments to delete.
Directory of rotated segments; empty keeps them beside the log.
Rotated segments older than this are deleted once their checkpoint is written.

The components the server expects to hear from. A declared Surveyor with fewer live replicas than min_replicas is degraded, one with none is silent (an alarm in the components view; /health and /ready do not change); for the first minutes after a start it is starting. Absent or empty: no expectation and no alarm. YAML only (a list of mappings has no environment or flag form), and the Helm chart does not render it yet.
What is expected. Only surveyor in this release; an unknown kind refuses the start.
The Surveyor's perimeter (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 40), unique per kind.
The KBs the component must cover; each must be a mounted KB, so a typo cannot silence the alarm.
Live replicas below which the component is degraded.

The read-only store the pinned plugins are read from: <dir>/<name>/<digest>/, filled by cartographer plugin vendor. The server never writes into it and never fetches. Required when plugins is set. YAML only.

Plugins whose server side this server loads, by plugin name: the digest pinned here is the only consent. At start a tree whose digest differs, or a plugin that is missing, has no server side or cannot load here, stops the server with the plugin named; a changed plugin needs a new digest and a restart. Empty: the server loads no plugin. YAML only.
Tree digest of the approved plugin, as printed by cartographer plugin vendor. Required.
Set to false to skip the pin: the tree is not read, but the name and digest are still validated.
Scalar settings handed to the plugin, typed by the settings its manifest declares.
Serve the read-only Atlas UI at /ui/ and its API at /api/ui/v1 in HTTP mode. false removes both routes.

Where agent bug and idea reports go. github opens a prefilled issue on the public repository; off removes the offer lines from the served instructions and the hint on internal errors; an https:// URL template (it must contain {title}) points agents at an internal tracker. Nothing is ever sent by the server.
Serve the public read-only API at /api/v1 in HTTP mode, independent of web.enabled. Off by default: nothing is exposed until set.
Browser origins allowed to read /api/v1, each scheme://host[:port] (http or https, no path, no *). Empty allows none.
Concurrent event streams one token may hold open on /api/v1.
Concurrent event streams the server holds open on /api/v1.
Days a skill or agent may go unused by every client before kb_status.usage counts it as stale. A value under 7 is raised to 7 with a warning; there is no value that turns the signal off.

Scope word every skill and agent of this KB must start with, followed by a hyphen: acme requires acme-review-mr. A skill or agent without it is an artifact_unprefixed finding, and a write that introduces one is refused. Empty or absent: nothing is checked.

Branch Cartographer commits and pushes to, in place of the remote's default one; the first push creates it. Empty or absent: the remote's default branch. Only the settings.yaml committed on the remote's default branch counts: a change made on any other branch has no effect until it reaches the default one.
